summary: Beyond the food, these are the things Japan exports to the world — and why collectors, chefs, and designers make pilgrimages here.

items.name: Japanese kitchen knives
items.why: Sakai and Seki have forged blades for 600+ years. Tōkyō knife shops like Kappabashi Kitchen Town will engrave your name on the blade.
items.where_to_buy: Kappabashi (Tokyo), Sakai (Osaka), Seki (Gifu).

items.name: Washi paper
items.why: UNESCO-listed handmade paper, made from kōzo mulberry bark. Used for shōji screens, origami, and luxury stationery.
items.where_to_buy: Ozu Washi (Nihonbashi), Kamiji Kakimoto (Kyoto).

items.name: Ceramics (Arita / Kutani / Mashiko)
items.why: Each region has a 400-year porcelain or pottery tradition. Arita is painterly blue-and-white; Kutani is colourful gold-leaf overglaze.
items.where_to_buy: Department store galleries in Ginza and Shinjuku; annual Mashiko Pottery Fair in November.

items.name: Kintsugi (golden joinery)
items.why: Broken pottery repaired with lacquer dusted in gold — the crack becomes the feature. A philosophy as much as a craft.
items.where_to_buy: Workshops in Tokyo teach one-day introductory classes.

items.name: Japanese textiles + kimono
items.why: Nishijin-ori brocades, Yuzen dye techniques, indigo aizome. Modern makers are reworking them into everyday clothing.
items.where_to_buy: Nishijin Textile Center (Kyoto), Itchiku Kubota Museum (Hakone).

items.name: Japanese whisky
items.why: Yamazaki, Hakushu, and Nikka built world-beating distilleries from Scottish templates. Stocks are tight — allocations sell out at retail.
items.where_to_buy: Dedicated whisky bars (Zoetrope, Shot Bar Zoetrope) or department-store liquor floors.

items.name: Soy sauce, miso, sake
items.why: Each prefecture has its own fermented pantry. Small-batch shoyu brewers age soy in cedar barrels for two years.
items.where_to_buy: Akomeya Tokyo in Ginza; breweries across Chiba and Nagano.

items.name: Green tea (sencha, gyokuro, hōjicha)
items.why: Shizuoka and Uji in Kyoto grow the most celebrated leaves. Gyokuro is shaded for three weeks before harvest.
items.where_to_buy: Ippodo (Kyoto and Tokyo branches), Lupicia.

items.name: Wagashi (traditional confections)
items.why: Seasonal sweets made with bean paste, kanten, rice flour. Higashi (dry sweets) pair with matcha; namagashi (fresh) are sculpted seasonally.
items.where_to_buy: Toraya in Akasaka (400 years old).

items.name: Anime & manga
items.why: Over half of global animation output. Studio Ghibli, Toei, Madhouse, Mappa. Weekly manga print runs dwarf English-language book sales.
items.where_to_buy: Animate Ikebukuro, Mandarake Complex Akihabara, Tokyo Character Street in Tokyo Station.

items.name: Video games
items.why: Nintendo, PlayStation, Sega, Capcom, Square Enix. Tokyo Game Show every autumn draws 250k visitors.
items.where_to_buy: Super Potato (retro), Pokemon Centers, Square Enix Café.

items.name: J-pop, city pop, and jazz kissa
items.why: A deep musical lineage from 1970s city pop (Tatsuro Yamashita) to global acts like Hikaru Utada, YOASOBI, and a live-house scene in Shimokitazawa.
items.where_to_buy: Tower Records Shibuya, Disk Union, Jazz kissa cafés in Kichijoji and Yoyogi.

items.name: Stationery
items.why: Pilot, Tombow, Kokuyo, Midori, Sailor. Pens are tuned to fractional tip sizes; the paper is buttery.
items.where_to_buy: Itoya in Ginza (12 floors of pens and paper), Sekaido in Shinjuku.

items.name: Denim
items.why: Kojima (Okayama prefecture) revived selvedge denim when the rest of the world abandoned it. Kapital, Momotaro, Iron Heart.
items.where_to_buy: Okura (Daikanyama), denim floors of Beams and United Arrows.

items.name: Rail engineering
items.why: Shinkansen averages 27-second lateness per year. Maglev on the Chūō line prototype hits 600 km/h.
items.where_to_buy: The Railway Museum in Saitama; Kyoto Railway Museum.

items.name: Consumer electronics & audio
items.why: Sony, Panasonic, Nintendo define the high street; audiophile brands like Audio-Technica, Stax, and Luxman ship globally.
items.where_to_buy: Yodobashi Akiba (nine floors), BIC Camera.

items.name: Ikebana (flower arrangement)
items.why: Three major schools — Ikenobō, Ohara, Sōgetsu — approach arrangement as a spatial, minimalist art.
items.where_to_buy: Sōgetsu Kaikan in Akasaka offers English classes.

items.name: Origami
items.why: From children's cranes (senbazuru wishes) to Robert Lang's computational folds. Japan is the living archive.
items.where_to_buy: Origami Kaikan in Yushima; museum shops nationwide.

items.name: Shodō (calligraphy)
items.why: Practiced for concentration, not decoration. Many studios host 60-minute English-taught sessions for visitors.
items.where_to_buy: Various studios offer hotel-arranged classes.

items.name: Omotenashi (hospitality)
items.why: The register of host-guest relationship you will experience at every ryokan, good restaurant, and department store elevator operator.
items.where_to_buy: Ryokan stays are the clearest introduction.
